# #9167: the SHARED policy-verdict corpus.
#
# One file, read by BOTH the Go simulator's test (pkg/policymatch) and the Rust
# enforcer's test (userspace-dp/src/policy_verdict_corpus_9167.rs). It is the
# policy-tier equivalent of testdata/nat_match_prefix_corpus.txt (#7481).
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS. `show security match-policies` had no independent oracle.
# Where pkg/policymatch does not share code with the Go write path it mirrors
# userspace-dp/src/policy.rs's tier walk BY HAND, and a hand mirror drifts:
# #6505 taught the Rust junos-host gate the #4569 fragment-associated deny and
# touched userspace-dp/src/policy.rs, policy_snapshot_error.rs, policy_tests.rs,
# _Log.md and docs/feature-gaps.md -- NO Go at all. The Go simulator kept
# reporting PERMIT / "local delivery" for a host-bound fragment the box DROPS,
# and it was fixed 71 commits later by writing ANOTHER hand mirror (#6576),
# which re-creates the same dependency on someone remembering two places.
#
# THE ORACLE IS THIS FILE'S EXPECTATION COLUMN, and that is the whole point: it
# is authored from the Junos semantics and produced by NEITHER implementation.
# Go compiles the config and runs pkg/policymatch.Match; Rust parses the
# snapshot and runs evaluate_policy_result_with_icmp; each compares to the
# column. Neither calls the other, so neither can agree with the other by
# construction -- the vacuity the issue names.
#
# WHAT IS COMPARED, and it is deliberately the operator-visible triple:
#   action     permit | deny | reject   -- the verdict the show surface prints
#   policy     the matched policy NAME, or `-` for the default-policy verdict
# The Rust side additionally checks the runtime POLICY ID agrees with the id the
# Go side stamps, which is what makes `RuntimePolicyIDs` a CHECKED shared helper
# rather than an unchecked one.
#
# FORMAT
#   case <name> [lenient]   start a case. `lenient` (#17077) compiles with
#                            CompileConfigLenient and the generator emits the
#                            post-quarantine snapshot (see FORMAT).
#   set ...                  a config line (flat-set syntax, applied in order)
#   feed <name>=<cidr>[,...] a dynamic-address feed overlay entry (#17077):
#                            the live prefixes for <name>; an empty RHS is a
#                            present-but-empty overlay (match-none, #12965).
#   q <from> <to> <src> <dst> <proto> <sport> <dport> <action> <policy>
#   ... [frag] [icmp=T[/C]]  trailing key tokens (#17077): `frag` marks a
#                            NON-FIRST FRAGMENT (Go Query.NonFirstFragment,
#                            Rust l4_present=false; its ports are ignored) and
#                            `icmp=T[/C]` carries the packet ICMP type[/code].
#                            sport/dport `-` = OMITTED selector (#3330/#3415):
#                            Go nil port (constrained terms fail closed);
#                            Rust evaluates a present port 0, so a term
#                            covering 0 fires there but fails closed in Go —
#                            never combine `-` with a 0-covering term (use a
#                            concrete 0, as port-zero-range-17081 does, for
#                            that shape). proto `-` =
#                            OMITTED protocol (#3323/#12227): Go Match with
#                            Protocol="" asserts the authored (default-only)
#                            verdict; the Rust packet always carries a
#                            protocol number, so that side asserts the
#                            underspecified classification instead — no
#                            app-constrained rule fires for unknown protocol
#                            255 — and such a row must expect policy `-`.
#                            A zone absent from the snapshot maps to id 0 in
#                            Rust (never a panic); Go passes the name through
#                            to its unknown-zone arms.
#   A query whose <to> is `junos-host` is HOST-BOUND: Go routes it through
#   matchJunosHost, Rust through evaluate_junos_host_policy_l3_aware (whose `None`
#   is local delivery, written here as `permit -`).
#   end                      end of case
# Blank lines and #-comments are ignored. `-` in the policy column means the
# default-policy verdict (no rule matched). `content-rejected` as the action
# (policy must be `-`) asserts the fail-closed snapshot-rejection verdict:
# Go Result.ContentRejected, Rust parse_policy_state_with_counters refusing
# the snapshot.
#
# ADDING A ROW: add it here and BOTH languages assert it. A row only one side
# knows about cannot exist, which is the property two hand-maintained lists do
# not have.
#
# KNOWN GRAMMAR LIMIT (#10511): the `q` row carries no NAT translation fields
# and no scheduler/time fields, so translated-dst rematch (DNAT, inbound NPTv6
# via its DNAT-channel encoding) and scheduler-gated verdicts are INEXPRESSIBLE
# here. Those shapes are pinned instead by the Go rename-evaluator unit cells
# TestPolicyRenameEvaluatorHandlesDNATV4AndV6Rows10511,
# TestPolicyRenameEvaluatorRematchesNPTv6ShapedRow10511, and
# TestPolicyRenameEvaluatorHonorsInjectedSchedulerState10511
# (pkg/daemon/daemon_policy_rename_test.go), which drive the same
# policymatch.Match the corpus differentials bind.
#
# REMAINING INEXPRESSIBLE SHAPES (#17077): wire-level packet facts the row has
# no field for — IPv6 flow label, DSCP, TCP flags, TTL/hop-limit, IP options —
# and session state (established-flow fast path, scheduler wall-clock beyond
# the case flag above, NAT hairpin identity, ingress-interface host-inbound
# scoping). Those stay in the per-language cells that name them; a future
# dimension joins the grammar only as an optional trailing token, never by
# repurposing a positional field.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- tier 1
case exact-zone-pair-permit
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow then permit
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 permit p-allow
q untrust trust 10.0.2.5 10.0.1.5 tcp 1234 80 deny -
end

# The default-policy verdict on BOTH postures. Without the permit-all row a
# corpus can pass while the default action is hard-wired to deny.
case default-policy-permit-all
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 permit -
end

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- tier ordering
# First-match-wins WITHIN a zone pair: the deny is authored first and must win
# over the later permit for the port it names, while the permit still takes
# every other port. A reader that sorted or last-won would pass the first row
# and fail the second.
case first-match-wins-within-a-pair
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set applications application app-ssh protocol tcp
set applications application app-ssh destination-port 22
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-deny-ssh match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-deny-ssh match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-deny-ssh match application app-ssh
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-deny-ssh then deny
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow then permit
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 22 deny p-deny-ssh
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 permit p-allow
end

# An exact zone-pair (tier 1) OUTRANKS a scoped global (tier 4) that also
# matches the same tuple.
case exact-pair-outranks-scoped-global
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy zp-allow match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy zp-allow match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy zp-allow match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy zp-allow then permit
set security policies global policy g-deny match from-zone trust
set security policies global policy g-deny match to-zone untrust
set security policies global policy g-deny match source-address any
set security policies global policy g-deny match destination-address any
set security policies global policy g-deny match application any
set security policies global policy g-deny then deny
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 permit zp-allow
end

# A scoped global applies where its scope matches and NOT elsewhere. The second
# row is the one that fails if a scope set is read as the all-zones wildcard.
case scoped-global-applies-only-in-scope
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/2 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.3.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security zones security-zone dmz interfaces ge-0/0/2.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
set security policies global policy g-deny match from-zone trust
set security policies global policy g-deny match source-address any
set security policies global policy g-deny match destination-address any
set security policies global policy g-deny match application any
set security policies global policy g-deny then deny
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny g-deny
q dmz untrust 10.0.3.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 permit -
end

# An UNSCOPED global applies to every zone pair.
case unscoped-global-applies-everywhere
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/2 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.3.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security zones security-zone dmz interfaces ge-0/0/2.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
set security policies global policy g-deny-all match source-address any
set security policies global policy g-deny-all match destination-address any
set security policies global policy g-deny-all match application any
set security policies global policy g-deny-all then deny
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny g-deny-all
q dmz untrust 10.0.3.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny g-deny-all
end

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- wildcards
# `from-zone any` / `to-zone any` zone-pair rules (tier 2/3) and their
# precedence over the global tier.
case zone-pair-wildcards
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/2 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.3.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security zones security-zone dmz interfaces ge-0/0/2.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
set security policies from-zone any to-zone untrust policy any-to-untrust-deny match source-address any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone untrust policy any-to-untrust-deny match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone untrust policy any-to-untrust-deny match application any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone untrust policy any-to-untrust-deny then deny
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny any-to-untrust-deny
q dmz untrust 10.0.3.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny any-to-untrust-deny
q trust dmz 10.0.1.5 10.0.3.5 tcp 1234 80 permit -
end

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- addresses
# A source-scoped rule: the address book is part of the snapshot, and a reader
# that ignored the address match would permit both rows.
case source-address-scoping
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security address-book global address a-lab 10.0.1.100/32
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-lab match source-address a-lab
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-lab match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-lab match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-lab then permit
q trust untrust 10.0.1.100 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 permit p-lab
q trust untrust 10.0.1.101 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny -
end

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- named terminal action
# A named zone-pair policy's terminal reject must survive lowering as an active
# reject, not silently become a deny/drop. The reverse direction confirms the
# default permit posture remains independent of the named rule.
case named-policy-then-reject
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-reject match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-reject match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-reject match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-reject then reject
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 reject p-reject
q untrust trust 10.0.2.5 10.0.1.5 tcp 1234 80 permit -
end

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the #6576 escape
# THE demonstrated escape this corpus exists for. #6505 taught the RUST junos-host
# gate the #4569 fragment-associated deny and touched no Go, so the Go simulator
# reported PERMIT for a host-bound NON-FIRST FRAGMENT the box DROPS. A non-first
# fragment carries no L4 header, so the port-bearing `junos-ssh` DENY cannot match
# it and the walk falls through to the later permit -- UNLESS the skipped deny's
# L3 OVERLAPS the fragment, in which case the permit is failed closed and the drop
# is attributed to that deny. The last row is the control: a fragment whose source
# does NOT overlap the deny is still delivered.
case junos-host-fragment-associated-deny
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security address-book global address trust-net 10.0.0.0/8
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy block-host-ssh match source-address trust-net
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy block-host-ssh match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy block-host-ssh match application junos-ssh
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy block-host-ssh then deny
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy permit-host-all match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy permit-host-all match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy permit-host-all match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy permit-host-all then permit
q trust junos-host 10.0.1.5 10.0.1.1 tcp 1234 22 deny block-host-ssh
q trust junos-host 10.0.1.5 10.0.1.1 tcp 1234 80 permit permit-host-all
q trust junos-host 10.0.1.5 10.0.1.1 tcp 0 0 deny block-host-ssh frag
q trust junos-host 192.168.9.9 10.0.1.1 tcp 0 0 permit permit-host-all frag
end
# Second first-match shape (#10506): a narrow PERMIT first, a broad DENY
# second. The earlier case pins deny-first/permit-second; this one pins the
# mirror, so a reader that reversed the exact-pair walk (R-02) fails here
# whatever the action polarity.
case first-match-wins-within-a-pair-permit-first
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set applications application app-ssh protocol tcp
set applications application app-ssh destination-port 22
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-permit-ssh match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-permit-ssh match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-permit-ssh match application app-ssh
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-permit-ssh then permit
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-deny-rest match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-deny-rest match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-deny-rest match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-deny-rest then deny
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 22 permit p-permit-ssh
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny p-deny-rest
end

# Cross-bucket config order, deny first (#10506): a `from-zone any` deny
# configured BEFORE a `to-zone any` permit. For untrust->trust both match and
# the earlier deny wins; the other two rows pin each bucket alone. The corpus
# previously carried ONE wildcard rule, so no row could observe the merge
# order — a merge that read to-any first (R-03) permits the first row here.
case single-wildcard-tier-deny-first
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/2 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.3.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security zones security-zone dmz interfaces ge-0/0/2.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security policies from-zone any to-zone trust policy from-any-deny match source-address any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone trust policy from-any-deny match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone trust policy from-any-deny match application any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone trust policy from-any-deny then deny
set security policies from-zone untrust to-zone any policy to-any-permit match source-address any
set security policies from-zone untrust to-zone any policy to-any-permit match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone untrust to-zone any policy to-any-permit match application any
set security policies from-zone untrust to-zone any policy to-any-permit then permit
q untrust trust 10.0.2.5 10.0.1.5 tcp 1234 80 deny from-any-deny
q dmz trust 10.0.3.5 10.0.1.5 tcp 1234 80 deny from-any-deny
q untrust dmz 10.0.2.5 10.0.3.5 tcp 1234 80 permit to-any-permit
end

# Cross-bucket config order, permit first (#10506): the same two buckets with
# the config order reversed, so the to-any permit wins the contested row. The
# pair pins "earlier config order wins" for both polarities: a flipped merge
# (R-03) hands the contested row to the later rule in BOTH cases.
case single-wildcard-tier-permit-first
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/2 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.3.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security zones security-zone dmz interfaces ge-0/0/2.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security policies from-zone untrust to-zone any policy to-any-permit match source-address any
set security policies from-zone untrust to-zone any policy to-any-permit match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone untrust to-zone any policy to-any-permit match application any
set security policies from-zone untrust to-zone any policy to-any-permit then permit
set security policies from-zone any to-zone trust policy from-any-deny match source-address any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone trust policy from-any-deny match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone trust policy from-any-deny match application any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone trust policy from-any-deny then deny
q untrust trust 10.0.2.5 10.0.1.5 tcp 1234 80 permit to-any-permit
q dmz trust 10.0.3.5 10.0.1.5 tcp 1234 80 deny from-any-deny
q untrust dmz 10.0.2.5 10.0.3.5 tcp 1234 80 permit to-any-permit
end

# Excluded source address (#10506): the rule matches every source EXCEPT the
# listed address. The in-set source falls through to default-deny while any
# other source permits — pinning the inversion in the shared oracle instead of
# only in per-implementation tests.
case excluded-source-address-scoping
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security address-book global address a-lab 10.0.1.100/32
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-nonlab match source-address a-lab
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-nonlab match source-address-excluded
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-nonlab match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-nonlab match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-nonlab then permit
q trust untrust 10.0.1.100 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny -
q trust untrust 10.0.1.101 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 permit p-nonlab
end

# ICMP is a first-class application protocol even when the packet carries no
# TCP/UDP ports. The unknown application row keeps a policy reader from
# defaulting every non-TCP tuple to a port-bearing deny.
case icmp-unknown-application
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set applications application app-icmp protocol icmp
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-icmp match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-icmp match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-icmp match application app-icmp
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-icmp then permit
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 icmp 0 0 permit p-icmp
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 udp 0 0 deny -
end

# The policy evaluator remains family-typed: the v4-only source deny catches
# plain IPv4, while mapped/compatible source and destination tuples reach the
# explicit permit-any inside policy evaluation. Issue #10686's ingress gate
# drops these embedded-v4 forms BEFORE policy; this corpus records the policy-
# core verdict the bypass reached, not the end-to-end packet disposition.
case embedded-v4-ipv6-policy-family-10686
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet6 address 2001:db8:1::1/64
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet6 address 2001:db8:2::1/64
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy deny-v4-source match source-address 10.0.0.0/8
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy deny-v4-source match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy deny-v4-source match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy deny-v4-source then deny
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy permit-any match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy permit-any match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy permit-any match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy permit-any then permit
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 udp 1234 80 deny deny-v4-source
q trust untrust ::ffff:10.0.1.5 2001:db8:2::5 udp 1234 80 permit permit-any
q trust untrust ::10.0.1.5 2001:db8:2::5 udp 1234 80 permit permit-any
q trust untrust 2001:db8:1::5 ::ffff:10.0.2.5 udp 1234 80 permit permit-any
q trust untrust 2001:db8:1::5 ::10.0.2.5 udp 1234 80 permit permit-any
end

# #17081: a literal port 0 is a PRESENT port in both halves — the Go corpus
# reader builds PortPtr(0) and the Rust reader passes u16 0 with
# l4_present=true, so a `0-1023` deny term matches it (the #13920 shape).
# The control row (dport 53) hits the same deny; a query port outside the
# range (2000) falls through to the permit-all rule behind it.
case port-zero-range-17081
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
set applications application app-low protocol udp
set applications application app-low destination-port 0-1023
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy d match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy d match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy d match application app-low
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy d then deny
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 udp 40000 0 deny d
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 udp 40000 53 deny d
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 udp 40000 2000 permit -
end

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- #17077 grammar

# #13705 transit frag + reject: a non-first fragment SKIPS the port-bearing
# REJECT (junos-https) but its L3 overlaps, so the later permit is overridden
# to the reject (the verdict label preserves the rule action). The control row
# is the same fragment from a source outside the reject's L3 scope.
case transit-fragment-reject-13705
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security address-book global address trust-net 10.0.0.0/8
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy reject-https match source-address trust-net
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy reject-https match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy reject-https match application junos-https
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy reject-https then reject
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy permit-all match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy permit-all match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy permit-all match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy permit-all then permit
q trust untrust 10.1.2.3 203.0.113.9 tcp 0 0 reject reject-https frag
q trust untrust 192.168.9.9 203.0.113.9 tcp 0 0 permit permit-all frag
end

# #11067 unknown-zone EGRESS: the to-zone is absent from the config/snapshot
# (Rust id 0, resolved egress), so the verdict is the unconditional unzoned-
# egress deny — NOT the default permit-all behind it.
case unknown-zone-egress-11067
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
q trust nowhere 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny -
end

# #8318 unknown-zone INGRESS: the from-zone is absent (Rust id 0), so the
# verdict is the unconditional unzoned-ingress deny, not default permit-all.
case unknown-zone-ingress-8318

set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0

q bogus untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny -
end

# #11369 unknown-zone junos-host, from-any precedence: an unzoned ingress
# still reaches the from-zone any -> junos-host and global tiers. Both rows
# here are decided by the from-any deny, so this case pins substitute-name
# precedence ONLY — the global tier is pinned alone by
# unknown-zone-junos-host-global-only-11369 below.
case unknown-zone-junos-host-global-11369
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
set security policies from-zone any to-zone junos-host policy block-unzoned match source-address any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone junos-host policy block-unzoned match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone junos-host policy block-unzoned match application any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone junos-host policy block-unzoned then deny
set security policies global policy block-global-unzoned match from-zone any
set security policies global policy block-global-unzoned match to-zone junos-host
set security policies global policy block-global-unzoned match source-address any
set security policies global policy block-global-unzoned match destination-address any
set security policies global policy block-global-unzoned match application any
set security policies global policy block-global-unzoned then deny
q bogus junos-host 10.0.1.5 10.0.1.1 tcp 1234 22 deny block-unzoned
q trust junos-host 10.0.1.5 10.0.1.1 tcp 1234 22 deny block-unzoned
end

# #11369 unknown-zone junos-host, GLOBAL TIER ALONE: no from-zone any
# junos-host rule exists, so both rows can only be decided by the global
# block-global-unzoned deny. Removing or breaking the global tier in
# either evaluator falls through to default permit-all and reds both
# halves on both rows; the from-any (substitute-name) tier is pinned by
# unknown-zone-junos-host-global-11369 above.
case unknown-zone-junos-host-global-only-11369
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
set security policies global policy block-global-unzoned match from-zone any
set security policies global policy block-global-unzoned match to-zone junos-host
set security policies global policy block-global-unzoned match source-address any
set security policies global policy block-global-unzoned match destination-address any
set security policies global policy block-global-unzoned match application any
set security policies global policy block-global-unzoned then deny
q bogus junos-host 10.0.1.5 10.0.1.1 tcp 1234 22 deny block-global-unzoned
q trust junos-host 10.0.1.5 10.0.1.1 tcp 1234 22 deny block-global-unzoned
end

# ICMP type/code: junos-icmp-ping is echo-request (type 8) only. Row 2 (type
# 0 echo-reply) and row 3 (no icmp= token: type not carried, fail-closed for
# the constrained term) both fall through to the default deny.
case icmp-type-code
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-icmp-ping match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-icmp-ping match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-icmp-ping match application junos-icmp-ping
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-icmp-ping then permit
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 icmp 0 0 permit p-icmp-ping icmp=8/0
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 icmp 0 0 deny - icmp=0/0
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 icmp 0 0 deny -
end

# Omitted selectors: `-` never matches a constrained term. Row 1 (no protocol)
# cannot hit the tcp/80 permit; row 2 (no dport, #3330) cannot hit it either;
# row 3 (no sport, #3415) cannot hit the source-port-constrained deny.
case omitted-selectors
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
set applications application app-web protocol tcp
set applications application app-web destination-port 80
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-web match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-web match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-web match application app-web
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-web then permit
set applications application app-sport protocol tcp
set applications application app-sport source-port 1234
set applications application app-sport destination-port 25
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-sport match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-sport match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-sport match application app-sport
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-sport then deny
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 - 1234 80 permit -
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 - permit -
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp - 25 permit -
end

# Feed overlay (#12965/#14337): the feed line supplies the live prefixes for
# the dynamic-address binding. Row 1's source is inside the feed, so the deny
# fires; row 2's source is outside it and falls through to the later permit.
case feed-overlay-12965
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security dynamic-address feed-server threat url https://feeds.example/list.txt
set security dynamic-address feed-server threat feed-name malware path /malware.txt
set security dynamic-address address-name bad-actors profile feed-name malware
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy deny-feed match source-address bad-actors
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy deny-feed match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy deny-feed match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy deny-feed then deny
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy later-permit match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy later-permit match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy later-permit match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy later-permit then permit
feed bad-actors=198.51.100.0/24
q trust untrust 198.51.100.7 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny deny-feed
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 permit later-permit
end

# Lenient quarantine (#5649): zzq17760/zzq8100 collide under StableZoneID, so
# the lenient path quarantines the later-sorting zzq8100 — its zone and its
# permit are absent from the published snapshot, and a query from it is the
# unzoned-ingress deny. The survivor zzq17760 still permits.
case lenient-quarantine-5649 lenient
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone zzq17760 interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone zzq8100 interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security policies from-zone zzq8100 to-zone trust policy q-permit match source-address any
set security policies from-zone zzq8100 to-zone trust policy q-permit match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone zzq8100 to-zone trust policy q-permit match application any
set security policies from-zone zzq8100 to-zone trust policy q-permit then permit
set security policies from-zone zzq17760 to-zone trust policy s-permit match source-address any
set security policies from-zone zzq17760 to-zone trust policy s-permit match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone zzq17760 to-zone trust policy s-permit match application any
set security policies from-zone zzq17760 to-zone trust policy s-permit then permit
q zzq8100 trust 10.0.2.5 10.0.1.5 tcp 1234 80 deny -
q zzq17760 trust 10.0.1.5 10.0.1.9 tcp 1234 80 permit s-permit
end

# Content-rejected (#3727): the policy names an application whose
# destination-port (70000) the snapshot builder cannot represent, so the
# WHOLE config fails closed. Strict commit rejects the port; the lenient path
# loads it and the dataplane refuses the snapshot — Go ContentRejected, Rust
# parse_policy_state_with_counters refusing it. Either arm reds if the
# fail-closed posture regresses to the default permit-all.
case content-rejected-3727 lenient
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
set applications application badport protocol tcp
set applications application badport destination-port 70000
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-bad match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-bad match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-bad match application badport
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-bad then permit
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 content-rejected -
end
